newsitem.title: NORWAY: SAS to cut costs by NOK 1 bln - report.
newsitem.headline: SAS to cut costs by NOK 1 bln - report.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) will release plans to cut costs by at least one billion crowns when it presents third-quarter results on November 19, the financial daily Finansavisen said on Thursday.
The reductions, which will include shedding jobs, will take place over the next two years and will affect all areas of the company, Finansavisen said.

SAS spokesman Peter Forsman confirmed to the daily that the company would announce a cost-cutting programme along with its results and that the measures would impact all levels in the airliner group. He declined to give any further details.
Finansavisen said SAS would implement the programme following announcements by its main rivals -- British Airways, Lufthansa and Dutch airliner KLM -- of a series of cost reduction measures.
SAS has already said that it does not expect to match 1995's record pre-tax profit of 2.6 billion Swedish crowns in 1996.

In the company's magazine in October, Scandinavian routes manager Knut Solberg said the company needed to increase profitability and freeze employment to get out of its "critically negative" financial situation.
The group's earnings were static in the first half of 1996 but spending rose by three percent.
